newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria plans index-linked T-bill issues.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria plans index-linked T-bill issues.

text.p: Bulgaria plans to issue index-linked T-bills, with yield pegged to the inflation rate, hoping to attract non-financial companies and individuals, finance ministry officials said.
"The project, which is still in a preliminary stage is aimed at shielding investors' money against inflation more effectively," an official who declined to be named told Reuters.

The index-linked short-term T-bills could also be an effective anti-inflationary instrument as they could attract money that people have withdrawn from banks amid current crisis of confidence in the banking system, the official added.

The principal of the T-bills could track the inflation rate reported by the National Statistics Institute and they could have a coupon of some three to six percent, the state news agency BTA quoted a ministry official as saying.

Now the ministry offers T-bills with maturity of three, six and twelve months and floater coupons set from 15 points below the central interest rate (CIR) to 25 points over CIR to firms and individuals.
The cumulative annual yield of these issues is around 130 percent under the current record high CIR of 108 percent, central bank data shows.
Monthly inflation for August was 17.1 percent after it leapt to 23.3 percent in July due to a drastic rise in energy prices.
Cumulative inflation for the first eight months was 113 percent, already topping the annual inflation target of 104 percent in the central government budget.
